qa.question: Should unit 4 capacity stay at 426 MW or change to 594 MW?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 594.0 MW nameplate for generator 4, and the Southwest Power Pool queue entry GEN-2024-GR5 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive) lists 594 MW as a gas and storage hybrid. The owner's dedication article (https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/grand-river-dam-authority-formally-dedicates-unit-4-grand-river-energy-center) says 426 MW. A 2024 permit memo (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8824.pdf) lists a 453 MW turbine.
qa.recommendation: Leave 426 MW for now. If the generator nameplate is 594 MW, change it to 594.
qa.note: The three numbers describe different ratings. Queue entry GEN-2024-GR5 is a replacement request, with a cessation date of 16 September 2026 and a summer rating of 554 MW against a winter rating of 594 MW in the open list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, read on 5 November 2026. That points to ratings that change with the season, not to extra storage capacity. A rating of 594 MW is a winter figure.

qa.question: Which older unit did unit 3 replace?
qa.finding: A Black and Veatch project page (https://www.bv.com/projects/power-plant-replacement-project-brings-price-certainties-cleaner-air) names the project Grand River Energy Center Units 2 and 3, which suggests the combined cycle replaced older unit 2. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 still lists a coal unit 2 as operating at 594 MW.
qa.recommendation: Find the GEM unit ID of the coal unit 2 at this plant and, if it exists, put it in the replacement link for unit 3. If no unit 2 record exists, ask the project manager whether to add one.
qa.note: I could not read the GEM unit ID for unit 2 from the brief. I did not find a document that says plainly which unit unit 3 replaced.

qa.question: Is Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2025-SR19 at the Maid 161 kV substation part of the Grand River Energy Center?
qa.finding: The request is for 100 MW, owned by the Grand River Dam Authority, with no fuel shown, near Chouteau, with commercial operation in November 2029 in the open list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, read on 5 November 2026. The Grand River Energy Center connects at its own 345 kV substation, which is a different connection point.
qa.recommendation: Keep GEN-2025-SR19 as its own new project and add no unit at the Grand River Energy Center.
qa.note: The queue list gives no site address or project name for this request. I found no air permit or board document that places it at the Grand River Energy Center.
